answer: Each identity must prove it runs on a distinct machine, checked by latency probes from several locations, and identities clustered on one host are capped and paid as one. A beacon station at an oasis cannot share a server with another identity and collect twice. An attacker wanting 1,000 identities must rent 1,000 machines and connections at 12 dollars a month each, spending 12,000 dollars a month before any earns a cent, even for machines crushing basalt all day. It is like a market giving one stall per street address.
